A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FGPS and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and full supplementary material. Content can be matched across the section reorganization and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic approximation-gap experiments, FFHQ and ImageNet restoration results, runtime measurements, and curriculum and step-size ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports an additional FGPS synthetic-error curve for filter width 10.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same sampling updates, Tweedie estimate, time-varying frequency mask, and measurement guidance. The frequency and step-size schedules are unchanged; added comments and theoretical expressions do not establish a changed restoration procedure.

E1.justification: FFHQ, ImageNet, and the four image-restoration tasks remain unchanged. v2 removes the low-pass synthetic plots and describes a high-pass study, but Appendix E.3 still mentions both operators. It is unclear whether synthetic coverage was narrowed or only its reported results.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Score-SDE/ILVR, MCG, DPS, and DSG; Table 2 retains DoubleDIP, AOD-Net, DPS, and DSG. The synthetic comparison remains FGPS versus DPS. Citation renumbering does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The documented image counts, resolutions, noise levels, pretrained models, metrics, sampling schedules, and task hyperparameters remain unchanged. Synthetic data generation also remains unchanged; filter width 10 already appeared in v1's DPS evaluation, and v2 adds FGPS results at that setting.

E4.justification: The synthetic sensitivity analysis drops the low-pass comparisons and extends the FGPS high-pass curves to width 10. The fixed-versus-varying curriculum, linear-versus-exponential schedule, and step-size ablations remain unchanged. The new main-text measurement visualization redisplays existing appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions average synthetic approximation gaps over 10,000 signals and retain the same statistical reporting practices. No changed seed counts, repeated-run information, uncertainty definitions, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds the FGPS high-pass result for width 10 and omits the low-pass curves shown in v1 Figures 2–3. Tables 1–4 retain the same numerical results, and the existing qualitative restoration examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 and its proof now explicitly include the FGPS score with the Gamma_t factor; DPS is restated as Corollary 3. New Appendix C adds an eigenvalue/projection argument comparing FGPS with DPS. However, v1's Gamma_t-free FGPS expression survives as v2 Equation 45, leaving an inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions explicitly recast the theoretical contribution around FGPS's approximation error and its advantage in selected cases, whereas v1 foregrounded exact characterization of existing methods' errors. The proposed frequency curriculum and main restoration-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 expands the frequency-mismatch and dataset-complexity explanations. Appendix H newly acknowledges that the Gaussian analysis does not fully explain practical Tweedie estimates or gains on complex datasets. Existing limitations concerning step-size tuning, image-valued measurements, and known forward operators remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit FGPS source-code repository link in the abstract, whereas v1 only promised a future release. Implementation settings and baseline access information remain essentially unchanged. The older future-release statement still appears in v2's appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds Rissanen et al.'s work on inverse heat dissipation to support the coarse-to-fine motivation. Other research positioning remains largely unchanged. The corrected van der Schaaf and van Hateren reference identifies the same work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized: the method precedes the theoretical analysis, synthetic experiments move into that analysis, and real-image experiments are separated into setup and results. The abstract, contribution list, method motivation, and results discussion are extensively revised.

P2.justification: The two synthetic plotting figures are replaced by a single high-pass comparison with revised time-axis labels and legend. A crop of appendix Figure 7 becomes main-text Figure 4, and several displays are relocated. Table designs and most qualitative figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 offers clearer method presentation, a more explicit FGPS derivation, better acknowledgment of the theory's limits, and code-access information. These provide limited overall gains. The benchmark evidence is unchanged, low-pass synthetic comparisons are lost, and the disagreement between Theorem 2 and Appendix E.3 prevents treating the theoretical revision as a substantial improvement.
